description: Run the bounded copy-overlap LZ binary-division stage for maximal K-mismatch global repetitions.

source.title: Approximate Tandem Repeats
source.paper: Finding Approximate Repetitions under Hamming Distance
source.technical_report: INRIA RR-4163 (2001), section 3, Algorithm 1 and binary-division stage
source.reuse: Algorithm definitions and ideas only; package implementation and fixtures are clean-room.

contract.terminal_precondition: The last symbol occurs exactly once in the text.
contract.lz_factorization: Copy-overlap Lempel-Ziv factorization: each factor is the shortest prefix of the remaining suffix with no earlier occurrence, where earlier occurrences may overlap the current factor.
contract.block_rule: Partition the factor sequence into consecutive blocks of at most K+2 factors.
contract.recursion_rule: For each block interval [first,last] with first<last, choose mid=floor((first+last)/2), run Algorithm 1 on the interval at the head of factor mid, discard repetitions touching the interval's final factor head or containing its first character, then recurse on [first,mid] and [mid+1,last].
contract.output_scope: Union of the intra-block binary-division-stage outputs only; block-head and within-factor stages are excluded.
contract.maximality: A returned global repetition has length at least 2*period, at most K mismatching shifted pairs, and cannot be extended by one text symbol on either side while preserving the mismatch bound within its recursive interval.
contract.output_encoding: Little-endian signed-64 words [record_count,(start,length,period,mismatches)*record_count], sorted by start, length, then period.
contract.validation_order: Validate the complete input frame before checking output nullness or capacity; error results write no bytes.

output.encoding: little-endian signed-64 count followed by four signed-64 fields per record

workspace.accounting: The primary uses a 2,176-byte candidate bitset, fixed text and factor-boundary arrays, a bounded reverse view, and logarithmic recursion state; caller buffers are excluded.
